title: How often a factor appears in fatal crashes is a poor guide to danger
statement: Pedestrian crashes are {{descriptive/frequency_vs_severity|factor=crash_type;level=pedestrian|share_all_crashes|pct:1}} of police-reported crashes but {{descriptive/frequency_vs_severity|factor=crash_type;level=pedestrian|share_fatal_fars|pct:1}} of fatal crashes. Rain, wet roads, intersections and crashes involving teenage drivers are common in crashes but under-represented among fatal ones.
effect: Over-representation ratio (share of fatal crashes / share of all crashes): pedestrian ×{{descriptive/frequency_vs_severity|factor=crash_type;level=pedestrian|overrep_ratio|.1f}}, motorcycle ×{{descriptive/frequency_vs_severity|factor=any_motorcycle;level=yes|overrep_ratio|.1f}}, intersection ×{{descriptive/frequency_vs_severity|factor=junction;level=intersection|overrep_ratio|.2f}}, rain ×{{descriptive/frequency_vs_severity|factor=weather;level=rain|overrep_ratio|.2f}}.
uncertainty: Pedestrian ratio 95% CI {{descriptive/frequency_vs_severity|factor=crash_type;level=pedestrian|overrep_low|.1f}}–{{descriptive/frequency_vs_severity|factor=crash_type;level=pedestrian|overrep_high|.1f}} (CRSS design-based; FARS numerator is a census).
denominator: Numerator: FARS fatal crashes (census). Denominator: CRSS-weighted police-reported crashes.
robustness: Pooled over 2016–2024, the CRSS-weighted composition of fatal crashes agrees with FARS within CRSS 95% CIs for darkness, pedestrian involvement and single-vehicle crashes; not for motorcycle involvement (CRSS {{measurement/fars_crss_fatal_composition|YEAR=all;attribute=any_motorcycle|crss_share|cipct:1@crss}} vs FARS {{measurement/fars_crss_fatal_composition|YEAR=all;attribute=any_motorcycle|fars_share|pct:1}}) or young drivers (CRSS {{measurement/fars_crss_fatal_composition|YEAR=all;attribute=young_driver|crss_share|cipct:1@crss}} vs FARS {{measurement/fars_crss_fatal_composition|YEAR=all;attribute=young_driver|fars_share|pct:1}}; imputed vs reported age). For driver-age factors the FARS share is taken among crashes with known driver age.
limitations: Descriptive ratios; other circumstances are not held constant. Not a rate per mile travelled.

title: Adjustment reshapes which circumstances look dangerous
statement: Much of the excess severity of night-time crashes is accounted for by other recorded circumstances; rain-crashes are no less severe than clear-weather crashes on the same road surface, their lower crude severity being accounted for by wet surfaces (statistical accounting, not causal mediation); interstates reverse from riskier to safer than comparable roads; the excess severity of crashes involving older drivers is unmasked.
effect: 00:00–05:59 vs 10:00–15:59: crude RR {{severity/fatal_crude_vs_adjusted|factor=tod;level=00-05|crude_rr|ci:2}}, adjusted {{severity/fatal_crude_vs_adjusted|factor=tod;level=00-05|A_adj_rr|ci:2}}. Interstate: crude {{severity/fatal_crude_vs_adjusted|factor=interstate;level=yes|crude_rr|ci:2}}, adjusted {{severity/fatal_crude_vs_adjusted|factor=interstate;level=yes|A_adj_rr|ci:2}}. Driver 65+: crude {{severity/fatal_crude_vs_adjusted|factor=older_driver;level=yes|crude_rr|ci:2}}, adjusted {{severity/fatal_crude_vs_adjusted|factor=older_driver;level=yes|A_adj_rr|ci:2}}.
uncertainty: 95% CIs from Taylor linearisation (25 strata, 67 PSUs, 42 df), including uncertainty in the covariate distribution.
denominator: All police-reported crashes (survey-weighted); outcome = crash has a fatality.
adjustment: Model A: all pre-crash circumstances at once (time, light, weather, surface, road and speed environment, area, driver age mix, vehicle types, alcohol (imputed), speeding, year); for time of day, weather and driver/vehicle mix an association leaving out their downstream variables is also reported. Model B adds crash configuration.
robustness: For the fatal-or-serious (KA) outcome the night pattern (00:00–05:59: crude {{severity/ka_crude_vs_adjusted|factor=tod;level=00-05|crude_rr|ci:2}}, adjusted {{severity/ka_crude_vs_adjusted|factor=tod;level=00-05|A_adj_rr|ci:2}}) and the older-driver pattern (crude {{severity/ka_crude_vs_adjusted|factor=older_driver;level=yes|crude_rr|ci:2}}, adjusted {{severity/ka_crude_vs_adjusted|factor=older_driver;level=yes|A_adj_rr|ci:2}}) replicate; interstates are not riskier crude ({{severity/ka_crude_vs_adjusted|factor=interstate;level=yes|crude_rr|ci:2}}) but are safer after adjustment ({{severity/ka_crude_vs_adjusted|factor=interstate;level=yes|A_adj_rr|ci:2}}), and rain-crashes remain somewhat less severe with surface held fixed ({{severity/ka_crude_vs_adjusted|factor=weather;level=rain|A_adj_rr|ci:2}}). Year effects in every model; model B (adds a possible mediator) shown alongside.
limitations: Associations conditional on a police-reported crash; travel speed, vehicle mass and occupant health not recorded; residual confounding likely.

title: "Speeding" mixes a strong and a weak association
statement: Crashes in which a driver exceeded the posted limit or was racing are strongly associated with a fatal outcome; "too fast for conditions" — most of the police-reported speeding category — shows no detectable excess in the adjusted risk of a fatal outcome, a small one for fatal-or-serious outcomes, and concentrates on wet and icy roads.
effect: Adjusted fatal RR: exceeded limit / racing {{severity/fatal_speeding_type|level=exceeded_limit_or_racing|adj_rr|ci:1}}; too fast for conditions {{severity/fatal_speeding_type|level=too_fast_for_conditions|adj_rr|ci:2}} (vs no speeding). Fatal-or-serious (KA): too fast for conditions {{severity/ka_speeding_type|level=too_fast_for_conditions|adj_rr|ci:2}}.
robustness: Speeding × wet: for limit exceedance the ratio of RRs wet vs dry is {{interactions/pairs_fatal|pair=exceeded_limit x wet|ratio_of_rr|ci:2}}, imprecise and compatible with no difference; on the additive scale exceedance adds less risk on wet roads ({{interactions/pairs_fatal|pair=exceeded_limit x wet|ic|cix1000:1}} per 1,000), largely because of the lower wet-road baseline; for KA the deficit is present on both scales ({{interactions/pairs_ka|pair=exceeded_limit x wet|ratio_of_rr|ci:2}}). Quantitative bias analysis: with recording sensitivity 0.8 in fatal crashes, the limit-exceedance RR is still {{measurement/qba_grid|exposure=exceeded_limit;se_fatal=0.8;se_nonfatal=0.2;specificity=1|rr_corrected|.1f}} at sensitivity 0.2 in non-fatal crashes and vanishes only near 0.1 ({{measurement/qba_grid|exposure=exceeded_limit;se_fatal=0.8;se_nonfatal=0.1;specificity=1|rr_corrected|.2f}}).
limitations: Speeding is a post-crash police judgement and is recorded more completely in fatal crashes (FARS {{measurement/fars_crss_fatal_composition|YEAR=all;attribute=speeding|fars_share|pct:0}} vs CRSS {{measurement/fars_crss_fatal_composition|YEAR=all;attribute=speeding|crss_share|pct:0}} of the same fatal crashes). The type split is exploratory (not pre-specified).

title: The most robust severity associations involve objective circumstances
statement: Motorcycle involvement, pedestrian crashes, the speed environment (50+ mph), unlit darkness and heavy trucks show large adjusted associations; alcohol is strongly associated under every coding, although its size depends on the coding. Given that a pedestrian is struck, the risk of death rises steeply with the posted limit and is higher when the striking vehicle is an SUV or pickup.
effect: Adjusted fatal RR: motorcycle {{severity/fatal_crude_vs_adjusted|factor=any_motorcycle;level=yes|A_adj_rr|ci:1}}; 50–55 mph vs 30–35 {{severity/fatal_crude_vs_adjusted|factor=speed_limit;level=50-55|A_adj_rr|ci:2}}; unlit darkness {{severity/fatal_crude_vs_adjusted|factor=light;level=dark_not_lighted|A_adj_rr|ci:2}}; alcohol (imputed) {{measurement/alcohol_coding_sensitivity|period=2016-2024;coding=imputed (ALCHL_IM)|adj_rr|ci:1}}. Pedestrian death, 50–55 vs ≤25 mph: {{vulnerable/pedestrian_killed_contrasts|victim=pedestrian;outcome=killed;factor=str_speed_limit;level=50-55|adj_rr|ci:1}}; SUV vs car: {{vulnerable/pedestrian_killed_contrasts|victim=pedestrian;outcome=killed;factor=striking;level=suv|adj_rr|ci:2}}.
population: CRSS police-reported crashes (crash level) and struck pedestrians (person level), 2016–2024.
denominator: All police-reported crashes; for pedestrians, all pedestrians struck in police-reported crashes.
adjustment: Model A pre-crash set; pedestrian model adds pedestrian age, sex, location, light, speed limit and striking-vehicle type.
robustness: Alcohol: complete-case police coding {{measurement/alcohol_coding_sensitivity|period=2016-2024;coding=police, complete case|adj_rr|ci:1}}, stable across the 2019 coding break; the imputed coding falls from {{measurement/alcohol_coding_sensitivity|period=2016-2018;coding=imputed (ALCHL_IM)|adj_rr|ci:1}} (2016-2018) to {{measurement/alcohol_coding_sensitivity|period=2019-2024;coding=imputed (ALCHL_IM)|adj_rr|ci:1}} (2019-2024).
limitations: Impact speed, vehicle mass and front-end geometry not separately observed; exposure to being struck not measured.

title: Some combinations amplify each other; others commonly assumed to are not detected
statement: Among the 13 registered pairs, pedestrian crashes in unlit darkness show amplification on both the additive and multiplicative scales, and motorcycle crashes involving alcohol carry a large additive excess. Pedestrian crashes on 50+ mph roads show the largest additive excess, in an exploratory pair. Speeding × darkness and young driver × late night show no detectable interaction for the fatal outcome (absence of evidence, not evidence of absence); for fatal-or-serious crashes speeding × unlit darkness shows an additive excess.
effect: Pedestrian × unlit darkness: ratio of RRs {{interactions/pairs_fatal|pair=pedestrian x dark_unlit|ratio_of_rr|ci:2}}; additive interaction {{interactions/pairs_fatal|pair=pedestrian x dark_unlit|ic|cix1000:0}} per 1,000 crashes. Pedestrian × 50+ mph road: additive {{interactions/pairs_fatal|pair=pedestrian x high_speed_road|ic|cix1000:0}} per 1,000.
uncertainty: Design-based 95% CIs; Holm adjustment across the 13 registered pairs on each scale; exploratory pairs unadjusted.
adjustment: Standardised margins from model A (or B for pedestrian/angle pairs) with one product term per pair.
robustness: Refitted for 2016–2019 and 2020–2024 and for the KA outcome (reports/interactions.md).
limitations: Behavioural factors are recorded more thoroughly in severe crashes, which can create apparent interactions; objective circumstances are most trustworthy.

title: Crash involvement and crash severity are different problems
statement: In two-vehicle crashes, teenage drivers are over-represented as the culpable party, but crashes involving them are less severe. Drivers aged 75+ are also over-represented as the culpable party, and crashes involving a driver aged 65+ are more severe.
effect: Relative involvement ratio (quasi-induced exposure): age 15–20 {{exposure/relative_involvement|factor=age_band;level=15-20;stratum=all|rir|ci:2}}; age 75+ {{exposure/relative_involvement|factor=age_band;level=75+;stratum=all|rir|ci:2}}; alcohol (imputed) {{exposure/relative_involvement|factor=alcohol_im;level=yes;stratum=2016-2018|rir|ci:1}} in 2016–2018 vs {{exposure/relative_involvement|factor=alcohol_im;level=yes;stratum=2020-2024|rir|ci:1}} in 2020–2024 (coding break); police-reported {{exposure/relative_involvement|factor=alcohol_police;level=yes;stratum=2020-2024|rir|ci:1}} (2020–2024). Severity (adjusted association, model A): young driver RR {{severity/fatal_crude_vs_adjusted|factor=young_driver;level=yes|A_adj_rr|ci:2}}; driver 65+ {{severity/fatal_crude_vs_adjusted|factor=older_driver;level=yes|A_adj_rr|ci:2}}.
population: Drivers in CRSS two-vehicle crashes (no hit-and-run vehicle) with exactly one culpable driver, 2016–2024.
denominator: Non-culpable drivers (proxy for drivers on the road).
adjustment: Crude RIR, with adjusted ratios shown in the supporting table.
robustness: Charge-based culpability (impairment charges excluded) gives alcohol RIR {{exposure/relative_involvement_charge_based|factor=alcohol_im;level=yes|rir|ci:1}}. Alcohol is reported by CRSS coding period because the imputed field dilutes the contrast after 2019.
limitations: No mileage or trip exposure exists in the data; QIE assumes non-culpable drivers represent drivers on the road (the pool is dominated by drivers struck from behind) and unbiased coding of pre-crash actions; single-vehicle crashes are excluded.

title: Within the same vehicle, unbelted occupants die far more often than belted ones
statement: Given a crash severe enough to kill someone in the vehicle, belted drivers and front passengers died less often than unbelted ones in the same vehicle. The size of the difference depends on how truthfully surviving occupants report belt use.
effect: Fatality-risk reduction associated with belt use (double-pair comparison): {{matched/belt_effect|estimand=fatality_risk_reduction_belt_given_fatal_crash|estimate|cipct:1}}; conditional logit OR of death, unbelted vs belted: {{matched/clogit_coefficients|model=main;term=unbelted|odds_ratio|ci:2@or}}.
uncertainty: Crash-cluster bootstrap CI (double-pair); crash-robust CI (conditional logit).
population: FARS light-passenger-vehicle occupants aged 13+ in front or second-row seats with known belt use, 2016–2024; vehicles in which at least one occupant died.
denominator: Driver/right-front pairs (double-pair comparison); vehicles with discordant outcomes (conditional logit).
adjustment: Everything shared within the vehicle (crash forces, speed, vehicle, road); age, sex and seat in the conditional logit.
robustness: If 10% of belted survivors were unbelted the reduction would be {{matched/belt_effect|estimand=fatality_risk_reduction_belt_given_fatal_crash_misreport_f10|estimate|cipct:1}}; if 20%, {{matched/belt_effect|estimand=fatality_risk_reduction_belt_given_fatal_crash_misreport_f20|estimate|cipct:1}}. Vehicles with no unknown-restraint occupant give the same result.
limitations: Conditional on a fatal crash; assumes occupants differ only in belt use, age, sex and seat; survivor-reported belt use. Cross-crash CRSS ratios (crude {{person/lpv_killed_crude_vs_adjusted|factor=restraint;level=none|crude_rr|ci:1}}) are confounded by crash severity and must not be read as effectiveness.

title: The post-2020 rise in crash severity is only partly explained by the recorded crash mix
statement: The fatal share of police-reported crashes was higher in 2020–24 than in 2016–19. Changes in the recorded circumstances of crashes account for roughly 30–50% of the rise, depending on the model; the rest is a higher fatal share within the same circumstances, most clearly in speeding-related crashes.
effect: Fatal share {{trends/numerator_denominator|outcome=fatal;comparison=2020-2024 vs 2016-2019;quantity=fatal_share_base|estimate|pct:2}} (2016–19) vs {{trends/numerator_denominator|outcome=fatal;comparison=2020-2024 vs 2016-2019;quantity=fatal_share_comparison|estimate|pct:2}} (2020–24), risk ratio {{trends/numerator_denominator|outcome=fatal;comparison=2020-2024 vs 2016-2019;quantity=ratio_fatal_share|estimate|ci:2}}. Share of the rise accounted for by the recorded crash mix: {{trends/decomposition|analysis=model_B;outcome=fatal;quantity=composition_share_of_change_ref_P0|estimate|cipct:0}}; within-circumstance risk ratio {{trends/decomposition|analysis=model_B;outcome=fatal;quantity=risk_ratio_within_ref_P0|estimate|ci:2}}.
uncertainty: Design-based (Taylor linearisation, 42 df); the variance of NHTSA's single imputation of severity is not included.
population: CRSS police-reported crashes 2016–2024 with known imputed maximum severity; FARS fatal crashes (observed changes; the CRSS–FARS match in fatal totals is by construction).
denominator: Police-reported crashes of all severities (CRSS, weighted).
adjustment: Pre-crash circumstances and crash configuration (model B); composition effect from applying the 2016–19 model to 2020–24 crashes.
robustness: With the 2020–24 model as reference the composition share is {{trends/decomposition|analysis=model_B;outcome=fatal;quantity=composition_share_of_change_ref_P1|estimate|cipct:0}}; without coding-drift variables, {{trends/decomposition|analysis=sens_B_without_coding_drift_vars;outcome=fatal;quantity=composition_share_of_change_ref_P0|estimate|cipct:0}}; complete-case outcome, {{trends/decomposition|analysis=model_B;outcome=fatal_cc;quantity=composition_share_of_change_ref_P0|estimate|cipct:0}}. About half of the rise in the share reflects fewer reported non-fatal crashes ({{trends/numerator_denominator|outcome=fatal;comparison=2020-2024 vs 2016-2019;quantity=denominator_share_of_log_rise|estimate|cipct:0}}).
limitations: The within-circumstance part is a residual (unmeasured speed, recording changes, reporting changes). The 2023–24 excess over the composition-only expectation is significant only under the complete-case outcome. No exposure data; the rise cannot be attributed to any cause.

title: Police-recorded behaviours are measured differently by severity
statement: Alcohol testing is selective (killed drivers tested far more often than survivors), police reports miss alcohol, CRSS alcohol coding broke in 2019, restraint use is self-reported by survivors, and drug and distraction fields cannot support severity or trend analysis.
effect: 2023: {{measurement/fars_testing|level=national;YEAR=2023;status=killed|pct_alcohol_tested|.0f}}% of killed vs {{measurement/fars_testing|level=national;YEAR=2023;status=survived|pct_alcohol_tested|.0f}}% of surviving drivers alcohol-tested (FARS, observed). CRSS alcohol unknown in non-fatal crashes: {{measurement/unknown_by_year|field=alcohol;fatal=0;YEAR=2018|pct_unknown|.0f}}% (2018) → {{measurement/unknown_by_year|field=alcohol;fatal=0;YEAR=2019|pct_unknown|.0f}}% (2019) (CRSS, estimated).
uncertainty: FARS testing shares are census counts; CRSS shares are weighted.
denominator: Drivers in fatal crashes; police-reported crashes.
robustness: Quantitative bias analysis grid for speeding, limit exceedance and alcohol (measurement/qba_grid); belt-use misreporting sensitivity in matched/belt_effect.
limitations: Recording completeness itself cannot be validated against an external gold standard in this repository.

title: The database identifies no intervention effect
statement: Severity-pathway attributable fractions show where deaths concentrate and what share would not have been fatal had a circumstance been absent, holding everything else fixed. They are not lives saved by any programme: no enforcement, camera, testing or cost data exist in the archives.
effect: Severity-pathway fraction, limit exceedance removed: {{burden/attributable_fractions_fatal|shift=exceeded_limit_removed|af|cipct:1}} of fatal crashes.
uncertainty: Design-based 95% CIs on the model-predicted fraction.
population: CRSS police-reported crashes, 2016–2024; deaths scaled to FARS.
adjustment: Model A; counterfactual sets the circumstance to absent for every crash.
robustness: Under plausible under-recording of speeding in non-fatal crashes the speeding fraction shrinks towards zero; the alcohol fraction does not (burden/bias_sensitivity).
limitations: Omits crash-occurrence effects; assumes no unmeasured confounding and correct measurement; says nothing about whether an intervention can change the circumstance.
